name: Vellimalainathar Temple, Tiruthengur
deity: Shiva as Vellimalainathar (worshipped by Sukra, the silver planet), with the goddess Periyanayaki (Brihannayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tiruthengur, near Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Vellimalainathar — the lord worshipped by Sukra, the planet of silver — with the goddess Periyanayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, its legend tells of Sukracharya regaining his lost sight by worship here, and of the nine planets each setting up a lingam, giving the lord his 'silver mountain' name.

sections.history: Tiruthengur, often written Thiruthangur, lies about 18 km from Tiruvarur (some 22 km from Mannargudi) in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The lord here is Vellimalainathar, 'lord of the silver mountain,' and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Vellimalainathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Periyanayaki — also Brihannayaki, 'the great mother' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The temple is known for its association with the Navagrahas, the nine planets, each said to have installed a lingam here.
sections.legends: The sthala legend tells that Sukracharya, the guru of the asuras and lord of the planet Sukra (Venus), lost one of his eyes and came here to worship Shiva; by his devotion he regained his sight. Because Sukra is called Velli, 'silver,' the lord who granted him grace is named Vellimalainathar, 'lord of the silver mountain.' Tradition also holds that each of the nine planets installed a lingam here, making the shrine a place of Navagraha worship, and it is sought for relief from the afflictions of Sukra.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, along with special observance on the days of Sukra (Friday). Pilgrims seeking the grace of the planets and the Paadal Petra temples near Tiruvarur include Tiruthengur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruthengur the pilgrim comes to a shrine of planetary grace, where Sukra regained his sight and the nine planets worshipped. Before Vellimalainathar, lord of the silver mountain, and the great mother Periyanayaki, the visitor seeks the clear sight of body and soul in a quiet Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruthengur is about 18 km from Tiruvarur and 22 km from Mannargudi, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
